It tells the agent where data lives and what fields mean. It also says whether to use a field, how to use it, and where it came from. Here are the five jobs: Discover: generate ontologies from metadata and connect existing semantic models. Ground: give agents trusted meaning for metrics, entities and relationships. Validate: check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage. Expose: serve context through MCP, CLI and API. Learn: fold certified corrections back into the ontology. A Next.js 16 frontend handles the web UI and authentication on port 3000. A FastAPI backend with LangChain runs chat, NL-to-SQL and catalog APIs on port 3001. An ingestion worker writes embeddings on port 3002. Postgres with pgvector stores the catalog, the ontology and the vectors. Source databases can be Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake or DuckDB. Models are set through environment “triplets” of endpoint, key and model. Separate roles exist for reasoning, non-reasoning, embedding and reranking. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works. Bundled datasets include BIRD Dev (1,534 questions, 11 databases) and Mini-Dev (500 questions). FDABench-Lite adds 169 questions, and BEAVER defaults to a 100-question sample.
